formula_checks.name: isBond
formula_checks.why: The class, not the presence of a maturity date, determines whether the account is a bond. This matches the card’s stated spec and keeps a non-bond maturity-dated instrument from being treated as a bond by this predicate alone.

formula_checks.name: bondInfo
formula_checks.why: “Value (the balance)” is ambiguous because the owner defines bond value as statement market value excluding accrued interest. Missing face and rate are treated differently, but the card does not describe invalid or negative value handling beyond face ≤0.
formula_checks.should_be: Call the value statement market value, exclude accrued interest from it, and keep missing face/rate/accrued-interest fields explicitly not entered.

formula_checks.name: annualCoupon
formula_checks.why: The multiplication is right when face and rate are known, but “nothing when either was not entered” may conflict with the owner rule that a missing coupon rate means $0 annual interest and the app says so. It also does not distinguish a missing face from a missing rate in the output.
formula_checks.should_be: When both are known, face × rate; for missing rate, expose $0 annual interest with disclosure at the income figure, not an invented yield; missing face should remain unknown unless fallback-to-value is specifically intended for yearlyInterest.

formula_checks.name: yearsToMaturity
formula_checks.why: Anniversary-based years to maturity avoids dividing by 365.25 and gives exactly 1 on the anniversary; calendar-date logic ignores time of day.

formula_checks.name: currentYield
formula_checks.why: Current yield is annual interest divided by current statement market value, excluding accrued interest. It refuses when rate is absent or value ≤0, as required.

formula_checks.name: approxYTM
formula_checks.why: The first gate requires face value and rate even for a CD, but the next branch says a CD’s YTM is its stated rate because it is not priced at a market price. A CD without a separately entered face value may therefore be refused despite a known stated rate; the card does not settle that interaction.
formula_checks.should_be: For a CD, return its stated rate when the rate is known, if the owner confirms face value is not needed; for non-CD bonds, require maturity, unexpired status, face, rate and positive price, then solve using value plus accrued interest.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card formula; owner decisions DEC-2748b and DEC-3390.

formula_checks.name: bondSummary
formula_checks.why: Total face value treats every missing face as zero, although DEC-2748b says a face value never entered stays blank and the screen must say “not entered”. A sum may total known face values, but the missing face must not silently become a known zero.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum entered face values and separately identify bonds whose face is not entered; do not report a complete face total without an incompleteness notice.

formula_checks.name: couponIncomeAnnual
formula_checks.why: The formula includes all bond and CD accounts, while the purpose calls this annual coupon income across “individual bonds”. It does not settle whether CDs belong in this coupon figure or only in the separate interest-income figure.
formula_checks.should_be: Clarify whether CDs belong in the Bonds screen coupon summary; use one consistent yearlyInterest rule and disclose missing-rate $0.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card purpose vs formula; owner decision DEC-2748c.

formula_checks.name: interestIncomeAnnual
formula_checks.why: Past-maturity bonds/CDs are excluded, which matches DEC-2748d. However, an instrument with no maturity date is treated as not past maturity and may continue contributing interest indefinitely; the card does not say whether missing maturity means unknown status or active.
formula_checks.should_be: Exclude instruments known to have matured; if maturity is missing, retain the interest only if the product rule explicitly treats it as active, and disclose missing maturity.

formula_checks.name: bondRateSensitivity
formula_checks.why: The pricing-change approach and proportional rounding match DEC-2484c/DEC-2748f, and CDs are refused. It does not state how a negative or invalid yield-to-maturity / price-at-yield failure is surfaced, or how rounding handles values below $1.
formula_checks.should_be: Use same price model at baseline and ±1 percentage point, floor down-shift yield at 0.01%, add the change to statement market value, round in proportion to bond size, and refuse if required prices cannot be solved.

formula_checks.name: buildNetWorth
formula_checks.why: Assets minus debt is correct, but the card does not state how it carries forward missing account values or debt balances. A complete-looking net worth can violate the missing-balance rule.
formula_checks.should_be: Return known total assets less known total debt, with both components and explicit missing-value warnings; do not claim completeness if either side has unknown balances.

formula_checks.name: sumWhere
formula_checks.why: It sums existing balances, counts missing balances separately, includes negative values, and returns zero only when nothing passes and nothing is missing. This explicitly avoids treating missing as zero.

formula_checks.name: plural
formula_checks.why: The generic “add s” rule is not sufficient for irregular nouns or supplied plural forms unless every caller supplies the correct plural. Examples like “person/people” or “property/properties” could be wrong.
formula_checks.should_be: Use an explicit plural form when supplied; only append s as a documented fallback.

formula_checks.name: prettyDay
formula_checks.why: Parsing year-month-day as a calendar date rather than through timezone conversion avoids off-by-one-day errors; impossible/empty dates return no result.

formula_checks.name: priceAtYield
formula_checks.why: The discounting formula is standard for a yearly-coupon bond, but it uses face value in the principal cash flow without saying it must be present and positive. It says coupon is zero when face/rate is missing, but an absent face still makes principal price undefined. Yield bounds/invalid yields are also unspecified.
formula_checks.should_be: Refuse when face value or maturity is missing/invalid; discount known coupon payments and face value at exact anniversary times; validate yield > −100%.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary bond-pricing arithmetic; owner decision DEC-3279c.

formula_checks.name: accruedInterestCaveat
formula_checks.why: It displays the owner-approved disclosure only when accrued interest is missing and an estimate is available; it does not add a caveat when actual accrued interest is entered.

formula_checks.name: isCertificateOfDeposit
formula_checks.why: Whole-word matching avoids false positives such as “CDW”, but the rule treats any occurrence of CD/certificate of deposit in the institution name as proof the account is a CD. An institution can have “CD” in its name without the account itself being a CD.
formula_checks.should_be: Prefer account kind or account-name evidence; institution-name evidence should only classify when the owner explicitly intends it to be sufficient.

formula_checks.name: rowOf
formula_checks.why: The row formula explicitly keeps face value and rate as “not entered” when missing, and uses the shared yearlyInterest/currentYield/approxYTM helpers for their stated refusal behavior. The rendered UI wording still needs runtime verification.

formula_checks.name: itemising
formula_checks.why: Keep-total-at, exact sum of known values, remainder and a nonfinal flag when any value is missing are coherent and align with the owner’s itemization decisions.

formula_checks.name: categoryEarnings
formula_checks.why: Category return is an average of holding returns weighted by current market value. The owner says every return must be time-weighted, and the retirement-return rule demonstrates the intended aggregate is weighted by beginning values (Σ ending / Σ beginning − 1), not current values. The formula can materially misstate a category’s return.
formula_checks.should_be: Calculate each category’s time-weighted return from the recorded values and flows over the requested period; if only holding-level returns are available, weight by beginning market value where valid, and refuse when the period cannot be measured.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule DEC-1669 and DEC-3035b; ordinary TWR practice.

formula_checks.name: windowStartKey
formula_checks.why: The basic date rules are explicit, but subtracting one, three, six, twelve or twenty-four months from dates near month-end/leap day needs a defined calendar rule. Native date arithmetic can roll into the following month rather than clamp to its last day.
formula_checks.should_be: Use a defined calendar-month subtraction rule (clamp to last day of target month where needed) and test Jan 31, leap day, and Since windows with future/empty records.

formula_checks.name: pricedGainOf
formula_checks.why: For a holding bought within the period, value minus cost is the gain; for other holdings, current value × (1 − 1/(1+r)) reverses a simple period return to infer the opening value and calculates price gain. It refuses for missing/nonpositive values or missing return.

formula_checks.name: investmentAccountIdsOf
formula_checks.why: The output is derived from the input accounts, whose IDs are unique by the account model; it includes an account once if its class is investment-related and excludes cash/property.

formula_checks.name: ledgerGroups
formula_checks.why: The class view correctly repeats split accounts at only their class portion and the institution view lists each account once. Missing balances and unknown class splits are not explicitly propagated, which can make the group totals look complete.
formula_checks.should_be: Rows and totals must reconcile to known values and visibly flag any account with missing balance; both views must add up to the same owned total when all data are known.

formula_checks.name: investmentRecordDates
formula_checks.why: It returns dates with at least one recorded value for the named investment accounts, oldest first, and empty when no accounts are named.

formula_checks.name: closedWith
formula_checks.why: The description says the record is returned unchanged when no earlier day exists or the latest earlier day contains none of the named accounts, while also saying it adds today’s value so a return can be measured. That is a potential contradiction: in the no-earlier-day case there is no base to append to, but the caller’s ending value may still be useful as a new point only if the contract says so.
formula_checks.should_be: Append today only when there is a valid earlier record for at least one named account; otherwise return unchanged and ensure caller refuses to measure a return. Clarify this explicitly.
